locus: praesentatione-beatae-mariae-virginis, Secret; editorial-projection artifact physical lines 24-27; antecedent 1862 Pustet: printed p. 580, text-layer lines 78985 and 78987-78992, under the heading Secreta. at line 78984. Line 78986 is empty in the layer and line 78987 opens with a stray I, which is the recogniser breaking up the ornamental initial; the initial itself reads FTlUa, for Tua,. The 1862 prints this Secret AT THE PRESENTATION ITSELF, in full, rather than by directive - which is what the calendar entry for this day already records. Read from the text layer alone. Its haec reads nsec, the characteristic damage this book does to the ae ligature after h; the word is confirmed at the same place by the Mame page image and by the 1962's own second printing.; target printed p. 722, no. 4132; artifact PDF p. 803, right column lines 6-12, under the heading Secreta at line 5 (which carries a marginal capital C - see notes).

text:
Tua, Domine, propitiatione, et beatae Mariae semper Virginis intercessione,
ad perpetuam atque praesentem haec oblatio nobis proficiat prosperitatem et
pacem. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et
regnat in unitate.
